summary:
I retrieved and quoted the observational and prior-art record on a spatially closed universe. All quotes are in facts.md. Derived numbers are in curvature_bounds.out and symbolic_checks.out. REPORT.md was not written because the harness refused report files, so this return carries its content.

Curvature data:
- The CMB alone prefers a closed universe. Planck 2018 TT,TE,EE+lowE gives Ω_K = −0.044 (+0.018/−0.015), with "only about 1/10000 samples at Ω_K ≥ 0". This preference weakens with the PR4 CamSpec likelihood and with ACT and SPT data.
- In ΛCDM+Ω_K, CMB+BAO now disfavours the closed side at about 2σ:
  - DESI DR2+CMB: 0.0023 ± 0.0011.
  - SPT CMB-SPA+DESI: 0.0027 ± 0.0012.
  - Giarè et al. 2026: P(Ω_k > 0) = 0.986.
- With w₀wₐ dark energy the closed side reopens. DESI DR2+CMB+SN allow down to Ω_K ≈ −0.0014 to −0.0019 at 95%, which means R_c ≳ 100–117 Gpc and more than 5×10⁴ Hubble volumes.
- DESI DR3 has not been released as of 2026-10-27.
- If closure is real, it is either below the cosmic-variance floor (about 10⁻⁴) or it falsifies eternal inflation (Kleban–Schillo; Guth–Nomura).

Prior art:
- The τ potential V₀[1+cos(τ/f)] is the Frieman–Hill–Stebbins–Waga 1995 PNGB potential, which the record never cites.
- Recollapse of a closed universe whose quintessence ends up oscillating in a minimum is published (Tipler et al. 2000/2007, crediting Barrow 1987).
- Born 1938, verified from page images, transfers Einstein's closed universe (radius a) to a momentum hypersphere (radius b) with independent constants. He does not derive closure from reciprocity.
- No source found derives closure from reciprocity.
- Scale-factor duality fails for Bianchi IX (Clancy, Lidsey and Tavakol 1998). My sympy check of tree-level dilaton gravity agrees. T-duality maps S³ to S²×S¹ with flux (Bouwknegt, Evslin and Mathai).
- Bigravity requires equal spatial curvature in both metrics (Comelli et al.). Curvature drops out of the scale-factor-ratio equation, so the aligned vacuum u = 1 survives k = +1.

[19S] check: the 93.8% is in the abstract. It is the sum of 12.2% (future dS→AdS) and 81.6% (already AdS today), for a Higgs-like quartic in flat FRW. #1 misdescribes it.

open: REPORT.md was not written: the harness refused the Write call ('Subagents should return findings as text, not write report files'). Its content is in this return; facts.md and the scripts and outputs are in the folder.
No published fit of cosine (PNGB) quintessence plus Ω_K to DESI DR2+CMB+SN was found. The w0waCDM+Ω_K closed-side edge (|Ω_K| ≲ 0.0014–0.0019) is only a proxy for the program's model.
ACT's R_k > 105 Gpc (closed, 95%) is looser than the Gaussian reading of its 0.0019 ± 0.0015 (137.9 Gpc). Their method is not stated in the passage retrieved.
The DESI DR3 release date is unverified. Only search-engine summaries of conference slides give one (late 2026/early 2027; April 2027), and I could not read the slide PDFs.
Born 1949 (RMP 21, 463) and Yang 1947 (PR 72, 874) were not retrieved (APS 403/paywall). Their content stays †.
The Higuchi and Fasiello–Tolley bounds are derived for de Sitter and spatially flat FRW. No closed-FRW (k=+1) version was found.
Lens-space (S³/Z_p) bounds exist only for |Ω_K| ≃ 0.02–0.05. Nothing was found at the |Ω_K| ≲ 0.002 still allowed.

Whether the program's second (polarization) frame f is FRW in the same coordinates as g is not settled in the record. If it is, Comelli et al. require it to be closed with g. If f were frozen and flat, a closed g would be excluded.
Barrow 1987 (PLB 187, 12), Barrow–Galloway–Tipler 1986 (MNRAS 223, 835) and Felten–Isaacman 1986 were not retrieved (†).

The record's 'Comelli, Crisostomi and Pilo 2012' is the perturbations paper, JHEP 06 (2012) 085. The FRW-with-curvature analysis is the four-author Comelli, Crisostomi, Nesti, Pilo, JHEP 03 (2012) 067.
record_errors: notes/broken-born-theory.md §7 item 3 says quintessence fits 'with a potential possessing a negative minimum find a 93.8% preference for a future transition to anti-de Sitter space'. In [19S] (arXiv:2506.21542) the fitted potential is a Higgs-like quartic V0 + ½m²φ² + ¼λφ⁴ whose minimum can have either sign. The 93.8% is the posterior probability that the vacuum energy is negative, and 81.6 of those 93.8 points are 'already being in an AdS phase today'; only 12.2% is a dS→AdS transition in the future. The fit assumes a spatially flat FRW background and is not a cosine potential. The quoted phrase itself does appear in the abstract.

papers/broken-born-checkpoint-v2.md §10 paraphrases [19S] as 'high posterior preference for a future anti-de Sitter transition and collapse in negative-minimum quintessence fits', which carries the same slant. [19S] fits a potential of either sign of minimum, and most of its AdS probability is AdS today, not a future transition.

Several wiki pages say the 93.8% figure appears only in #1 and has not been rechecked: wiki/cosmology/scale-factor-duality/conjugate-bounce.md 'Cautions', wiki/predictions/fate-of-expansion.md, wiki/cosmology/dark-energy/quintessence.md, wiki/cosmology/dark-energy/potential-sign.md, wiki/history/documents/lab-notebook.md and wiki/references.md. The figure is now verified verbatim in the [19S] abstract (v1 and v2), and these pages should say so.

Prior-art gap: the τ potential V₀[1+cos(τ/f)] (#11 §10, #1 §3/§7) is the Frieman–Hill–Stebbins–Waga 1995 PNGB quintessence potential, L = ½(∂φ)² − M⁴[cos(φ/f)+1] (PRL 75, 2077). No document in the record cites it. That paper's flat-universe result bears on flag 27: the field relaxes into oscillations that redshift like matter, so there is no flat turnaround.

Prior-art gap: review/round5-adjudication.md R11 ('A closed universe can turn around with V ≥ 0') is published mechanism. Tipler et al. (gr-qc/0003082; MNRAS 379, 629) give the case of quintessence oscillating about a quadratic minimum, crediting Barrow 1987. If the program adopts closure, the turnaround should be tagged [T] with these citations, not [D].

Not a record error but cited-adjacent: DESI DR1 (arXiv:2404.03002v3) prints Ω_K = −0.0024 ± 0.0016 in its Conclusions, while its eq. (24) and Table 3 give +0.0024 ± 0.0016 (open). Any record use should take +0.0024.
